claims.text: Resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion in high-entropy alloys is governed by formation of an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer.
The ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer is generated by mechanical-deformation-induced amorphization.
The ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer lowers friction.
The ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer promotes formation of a stable passivating oxide.
The passivating oxide mitigates chemical attack.
The proposed initial state can be a relatively coarse-grained CoCrFeMnNi alloy.
Controlled mechanical wear can trigger dynamic amorphization and grain refinement at the alloy surface.
The ultra-nanocrystalline layer has a high density of refined grain boundaries.
The near-surface layer has lower interfacial or grain-boundary energy.
Inverse Hall-Petch behavior in the refined surface microstructure favors low friction.
The refined microstructure encourages rapid formation of a passivating oxide layer.
The refined near-surface layer minimizes wear through an improved mechanical response.
Under combined wear and corrosion, the alloy will have a lower wear rate than the same alloy tested under inert wear conditions.
Under combined wear and corrosion, the alloy will sustain less corrosion damage than samples tested in an inert environment.
The protective ultra-nanocrystalline passivating layer will maintain its integrity when environmental conditions permit stable passivation.
The proposed benefits should fail when extreme pH or high temperature prevents formation or stability of the protective oxide.
Under inert wear conditions, dynamic amorphization and passivating-oxide formation are less critical to performance.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts reduced corrosion damage relative to an explicitly non-corrosive inert baseline. Because that baseline lacks corrosive exposure, it is not a coherent comparator for demonstrating reduced corrosion damage.

The mechanism treats deformation-induced amorphization as central to wear resistance, whereas the baseline description says it is less critical under inert wear. The cited evidence specifically associates low friction and wear in an inert environment with the ultra-nanocrystalline layer and dynamic-amorphization model.
